info.name: CNF — Submit MIGO (goods receipt against STO delivery)  [QS4/700 certified]
info.description:
Shree Cement CNF C&F Agent — Submit MIGO (v1.9 sheet MIGO-02).

RUNTIME-CERTIFIED ON QS4/700, 2026-08-25.
A single external deep insert created material document 5007138616 / year 2026 against purchase order 5600084238 item 00010 AND delivery 9004953150 item 000010 — 4 EA of material 17035056 into plant 1022, storage location FKGU.

Verified three independent ways:
  1. OData $expand readback returned the persisted item
  2. MSEG read directly in SAP: BWART 101, WERKS 1022, LGORT FKGU, EBELN/EBELP 5600084239/00010, SHKZG S, BUKRS 1000
  3. MSEG-VBELN_IM = 9004953150/000010 and KZBEW = B, matching the shape of the client's own MIGO_GR receipts

THE DELIVERY IS PART OF THE REQUEST. One purchase order line can carry many deliveries and a goods receipt is raised per delivery, so PO plus item alone is ambiguous. Send BOTH references together with GoodsMovementRefDocType = B. Sending the delivery INSTEAD of the PO is rejected — negative request B proves it.

SERVICE
  API_MATERIAL_DOCUMENT_SRV, plain path. ;v=1 is NOT required for this service.
  Base URL comes from the {{host}} environment variable.

SETUP
  1. Import this collection and CNF_SubmitMIGO_QS4.postman_environment.json
  2. Select the environment and put your own password in sap-pass
  3. Settings > General > SSL certificate verification = OFF (internal CA), or install the CA chain
  4. Leave cookie handling ON — the CSRF token is useless without its session cookie
  5. Run folder 0 first

SAFETY
  The posting request is gated by confirmSubmitMIGO. It refuses to run unless you set it to
  YES, and resets itself to NO after every response. There is no simulation mode in OData —
  a successful call creates a real, posted material document that must be reversed (movement
  102) rather than deleted.

EVERY request is labelled:
  [PROVEN]   executed against SAP, real response captured and saved as an example
  [MANUAL]   cannot be done over HTTP; do it in SAP GUI

item.name: 0 — Setup
item.description: Run this first. SAP Gateway rejects every POST without a valid x-csrf-token AND the matching session cookie.

exec: if (t) { pm.environment.set('csrf', t); pm.test('CSRF token captured', () => pm.expect(t).to.be.a('string')); }
else { pm.test('CSRF token captured', () => pm.expect.fail('No x-csrf-token header. Check host, credentials and that cookies are enabled.')); }

request.description:
Run this FIRST. Returns the service document plus an x-csrf-token header, which the test script stores in {{csrf}}.

Postman must keep the matching SAP session cookie — leave cookie handling ON. A token without its cookie is rejected, and the failure reads like an auth error rather than a CSRF error.

Proven 2026-08-25 on QS4/700: HTTP 200. The plain service path resolves; ;v=1 is NOT required for this service (unlike API_OUTBOUND_DELIVERY_SRV, which does require ;v=2).

item.name: 1 — Find an eligible STO item  [PROVEN reads]
item.description:
A goods receipt is posted PER DELIVERY, not per purchase order line. One PO line commonly carries many deliveries, so you must identify the delivery before you can post.

An item is receivable only when BOTH hold:
  (a) a goods issue (movement 641) has posted, so stock in transit exists, AND
  (b) that delivery has not already been received

Condition (a) CANNOT be checked over OData — the purchase order service exposes no goods-received quantity at all. Confirm it in SAP GUI: MB5T, or ME23N > item > Purchase Order History looking for VGABE=6 / BEWTP=U with movement 641.

exec: rows.forEach(r => console.log('  ' + r.PurchaseOrder + '/' + r.PurchaseOrderItem + '  mat=' + r.Material + '  sloc=' + (r.StorageLocation || '(blank - you must supply one)') + '  qty=' + r.OrderQuantity + ' ' + r.PurchaseOrderQuantityUnit));
pm.test('These are CANDIDATES ONLY - stock in transit still unverified', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);

url.raw: {{base}}/API_PURCHASEORDER_PROCESS_SRV/A_PurchaseOrderItem?$filter=PurchaseOrderItemCategory eq '7' and IsCompletelyDelivered eq false and GoodsReceiptIsExpected eq true and Plant eq '{{receivingPlant}}'&$select=PurchaseOrder,PurchaseOrderItem,Material,Plant,StorageLocation,OrderQuantity,PurchaseOrderQuantityUnit,IsCompletelyDelivered&$top=20&$format=json&sap-client={{sap-client}}

query.value: PurchaseOrderItemCategory eq '7' and IsCompletelyDelivered eq false and GoodsReceiptIsExpected eq true and Plant eq '{{receivingPlant}}'

request.description:
NARROWS the candidate list. It does NOT confirm eligibility.

The filter finds stock-transfer items (item category 7) that are not yet fully delivered, expect a goods receipt, and sit in your target plant. Executed 2026-08-25 against QS4/700 and returned 8 rows for plant 1022.

WHAT THIS CANNOT TELL YOU: whether stock in transit exists. A two-step STO receipt is only possible after the goods issue (movement 641) has posted at the supplying plant. That quantity is NOT exposed by this OData service — A_PurchaseOrderScheduleLine carries ScheduleLineOrderQuantity but has no goods-received quantity at all.

So most rows this returns will NOT be receivable. You must confirm stock in transit in SAP GUI — MB5T, or ME23N > item > Purchase Order History looking for a VGABE=6 / BEWTP=U row with movement 641.

Also note: rows with a blank StorageLocation need one supplied in the posting payload.

exec: console.log('Delivery items for PO ' + pm.environment.get('purchaseOrder') + ': ' + rows.length);

rows.forEach(r => console.log('  ' + r.DeliveryDocument + '/' + r.DeliveryDocumentItem + '  qty=' + r.ActualDeliveryQuantity + ' ' + r.DeliveryQuantityUnit + (Number(r.ActualDeliveryQuantity) === 0 ? '   <- parent of a batch split, do not post this one' : '')));
pm.test('One PO line can carry many deliveries', () => pm.expect(rows.length).to.be.above(0));

request.description:
THE DELIVERY IS PART OF THE REQUEST, so you must pick one. This lists every delivery item raised against your chosen purchase order.

Note how many there can be. Executed 2026-08-25 against QS4/700: STO 5600071885 item 10 returned roughly sixteen delivery items, 5600071018 about twelve. That is exactly why purchase order plus item alone cannot identify a goods receipt.

BATCH SPLITS: for batch-managed materials you will see PAIRS — a parent item 000010 with quantity 0.000 and a child item 900001 carrying the real quantity. Post against the item that carries the quantity.

This request still cannot tell you whether stock in transit exists for that delivery. Confirm the 641 in SAP GUI (MB5T, or ME23N > Purchase Order History) before posting.

item.name: Read the chosen purchase order + schedule lines  [PROVEN]

exec: items.forEach(i => console.log('item ' + i.PurchaseOrderItem + '  mat=' + i.Material + '  plant=' + i.Plant + '  sloc=' + (i.StorageLocation||'-') + '  cat=' + i.PurchaseOrderItemCategory + '  delivered=' + i.IsCompletelyDelivered));

request.description:
Inspect the chosen purchase order before posting: document type, supplying plant, item category, material, plant, storage location and scheduled quantity.

Use it to copy the exact Material, Plant, StorageLocation and unit into the environment. Material must be sent ZERO-PADDED TO 18 CHARACTERS in the posting payload.

item.name: 2 — Submit MIGO  [PROVEN — creates a real document]
item.description:
Run in order: the posting, then the readback. Both negative requests are safe and create nothing.

Before posting, set these from the delivery you chose in folder 1:
  material (18-char zero-padded), receivingPlant, storageLocation, quantity, unit,
  purchaseOrder, purchaseOrderItem (5-char, e.g. 00010),
  delivery, deliveryItem (6-char, e.g. 000010 - or 900001 for a batch split)

Then set confirmSubmitMIGO = YES. It resets to NO automatically.

exec: throw new Error('Submit MIGO blocked. Set confirmSubmitMIGO=YES only after confirming (a) stock in transit exists - a posted 641 - and (b) this delivery has not already been received.');
if (!pm.environment.get(key)) throw new Error(`Missing required environment variable: ${key}`);
if (String(pm.environment.get('purchaseOrderItem')).length < 5) console.warn('purchaseOrderItem is normally zero-padded to 5, e.g. 00010');
if (String(pm.environment.get('deliveryItem')).length < 6) console.warn('deliveryItem is normally zero-padded to 6, e.g. 000010 or 900001');
pm.test('SAP returned a material document number', () => pm.expect(d.MaterialDocument).to.match(/^\d+$/));
pm.test('Create response echoes no items - expected; run the readback', () => {

request.description:
CREATES A REAL SAP MATERIAL DOCUMENT. There is no simulation mode in OData.

TWO FIELDS DECIDE THIS CALL.

1) GoodsMovementRefDocType = "B"
   The OData equivalent of MVT_IND in BAPI_GOODSMVT_CREATE; B = goods movement for a purchase order. Omit it and SAP returns 400 saying PURCHASEORDER is not supported — which names the wrong field. See negative request A.

2) Delivery + DeliveryItem
   ONE PURCHASE ORDER LINE CAN HAVE MANY DELIVERIES, and a goods receipt is posted per delivery. Purchase order plus item alone does NOT identify which consignment you are receiving. Live QS4 data: STO 5600071885 item 10 has roughly sixteen deliveries; 5600071018 item 10 has about twelve.
   Sending the delivery populates MSEG-VBELN_IM / VBELP_IM, which is what the client's own MIGO_GR documents carry.

DO NOT send Delivery INSTEAD of the purchase order. RefDocType L with Delivery only is rejected — see negative request B. SAP wants BOTH references, with RefDocType B. That matches the client's live receipts, which all carry MSEG-KZBEW = B together with a populated VBELN_IM.

BATCH-SPLIT WARNING: for batch-managed materials the delivery quantity sits on the batch-split item (typically 900001), while the parent item 000010 shows 0.000. Send the item that actually carries the quantity. Two of the client's three sampled live receipts reference VBELP_IM = 900001.

CtrlPostgForExtWhseMgmtSyst is deliberately omitted; setting it can produce a delivery instead of a material document.

PROVEN 2026-08-25 in QS4/700: created material document 5007138616 / 2026 — 4 EA of material 17035056 into plant 1022 / FKGU, purchase order 5600084238 item 00010, delivery 9004953150 item 000010. MSEG readback confirmed KZBEW = B and VBELN_IM = 9004953150/000010.

item.name: GET created material document + items  [PROVEN readback]

exec: pm.test('At least one item persisted', () => pm.expect(items.length).to.be.above(0));

console.log('VERIFIED  mat=' + it.Material + '  plant=' + it.Plant + '  sloc=' + it.StorageLocation + '  qty=' + it.QuantityInEntryUnit + ' ' + it.EntryUnit + '  PO=' + it.PurchaseOrder + '/' + it.PurchaseOrderItem + '  delivery=' + it.Delivery + '/' + it.DeliveryItem);

request.description:
MANDATORY. The create response returns an EMPTY item array, so the posting is not verified until this returns the item.

The key is composite and THE YEAR COMES FIRST.

The readback echoes Delivery and DeliveryItem, so it is also your proof that the delivery link was stored. Note both PurchaseOrderItem and DeliveryItem come back UNPADDED ('10') although they are sent padded ('00010' / '000010'). Not a mismatch.

Proven 2026-08-25 for 5007138616/2026: mat 17035056, plant 1022, FKGU, mvt 101, refdoc B, PO 5600084238/10, delivery 9004953150/10, 4 EA.

response.name: 200 OK — item with delivery link, cross-checked against MSEG

exec: pm.test('SAP names the PO properties as unsupported', () => pm.expect(msgs).to.include('PURCHASEORDER'));

request.description:
SAFE — creates nothing. Identical to the posting request except GoodsMovementRefDocType is omitted.

Executed 2026-08-25 in QS4/700 on two different purchase orders, both returning the same rejection, so it is structural rather than document-specific. EKET was re-read afterwards and was unchanged.

  MM_IM_ODATA_API_MDOC/011  Property PURCHASEORDERITEM is not supported for GoodsMovementType 101

item.name: POST negative B — delivery INSTEAD of PO (RefDocType L)  [PROVEN rejection, creates nothing]

exec: pm.test('SAP rejects DELIVERY as a standalone reference', () => pm.expect(msgs).to.include('DELIVERY'));

request.description:
SAFE — creates nothing. This is the intuitive-but-wrong shape: reference the DELIVERY INSTEAD OF the purchase order, using GoodsMovementRefDocType = L.

Executed 2026-08-25 in QS4/700:

HTTP 400
  MM_IM_ODATA_API_MDOC/011  Property DELIVERY is not supported for GoodsMovementType 101
  MM_IM_ODATA_API_MDOC/011  Property DELIVERYITEM is not supported for GoodsMovementType 101

SAP wants BOTH references together with RefDocType B — not the delivery on its own. This request exists so nobody re-derives that the hard way.

Corroborating evidence: every sampled live receipt in QS4 carries MSEG-KZBEW = B (purchase order) AND a populated VBELN_IM (delivery). The delivery is an additional reference, not a replacement.

An HTTP 201 is the API telling you it succeeded. These checks are SAP telling you.
